neighbours.label: The second member of a stock opposite or complementary pair after 'and' or '&' (hot and [cold], low and [high], morning and [afternoon], Innocence and [Experience])
fire: Bathrooms are European standard, with hot and cold water and a private terrace.
The sensor measures low and high frequencies and reports them to the logger.
The Mercury brought out morning and afternoon editions throughout the twentieth century.
Close readings of Songs of Innocence and Experience gave students a feel for literary criticism.
The pipes supply an adequate and potable flow of hot and cold water to every flat.
Open day and night, the shop serves rich and poor customers alike.
She walked between the old and new parts of the city, past young and old alike.
The report covers supply and demand in the spring and autumn markets.
quiet: Bathrooms are European standard, with hot and spicy tea and a private terrace.
The sensor measures low and shallow readings and reports them to the logger.
The Mercury brought out morning and weekly editions throughout the twentieth century.
Close readings of Songs of Innocence and Wonder gave students a feel for literary criticism.
The pipes supply an adequate and potable flow of clean and safe water to every flat.
Open day and night, the shop serves rich and tasty meals to customers.
She walked between the old and quiet parts of the city, past young and happy families.
The report covers supply and cost in the spring and autumn markets.

short: second half of 'X and Y' pair
